quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: A driver entering freeway traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp:

options.text: Has the right-of-way.
Should yield to drivers already on the freeway.
May force their way into traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the freeway.
questions.explanation: When entering a freeway from a ramp, you must yield to drivers already on the freeway. Merge safely when there is a gap in traffic.

questions.question: To pass on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Judge the distance to any oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judge the distance to any oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming vehicles are traveling. Before passing, make sure you have enough space and time to change lanes safely. Wait to pass if you are unsure about an oncoming vehicle's speed.

questions.question: It is more dangerous to drive at night than during the day because:

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead at night.
The road is always more slippery at night.
Your reaction time is slower at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead at night.
questions.explanation: At night, you can see less far ahead. Headlight glare from oncoming vehicles makes this worse. Always use your headlights and drive with extra caution in the dark.

questions.question: Trucks' blind spots are:

options.text: Directly behind the body.
On the immediate left of the cab.
Both on the immediate left of the cab and directly behind the body.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both on the immediate left of the cab and directly behind the body.
questions.explanation: Trucks have much larger blind spots than cars. The truck driver cannot see your car behind or to the side of the truck. If you cannot see the driver's face in their mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: If you are driving on a highway next to a single broken white line marking:

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass.
You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross a dashed white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When entering traffic after being parked at a curb, you:

options.text: Should drive more slowly than other traffic for 200 feet.
Should wait for a large enough gap to get up to the speed of traffic.
Should wait for the first two vehicles to pass, then drive into the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should wait for a large enough gap to get up to the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging into traffic, wait for a gap that is large enough for your vehicle to match the speed of other traffic.

questions.question: Which of the following road surfaces freezes first?

options.text: A tunnel
An intersection
A bridge

questions.correctAnswerText: A bridge
questions.explanation: Bridges and overpasses freeze before other road surfaces. They also thaw out later than regular pavement.

questions.question: Prior to entering a curve:

options.text: Activate your turn signal.
Reduce your speed.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: You may drive slower than the posted speed limit for safety. Reduce speed when approaching curves, hills with limited visibility, slippery roads, or areas with pedestrians and animals.

questions.question: Extra space in front of a large truck is needed for:

options.text: Other drivers to merge onto the freeway.
The truck driver to stop the vehicle.
Other drivers when they want to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck driver to stop the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Trucks take much longer to stop than cars. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on a thin film of water instead of on the road. To prevent hydroplaning in wet weather, you should:

options.text: Put on your cruise control to maintain a constant speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it starts to rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slow down when driving on wet pavement to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: To see vehicles in your blind spots, you should check:

options.text: The inside rearview mirror.
The outside rearview mirror.
Over your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots cannot be seen in mirrors by definition. Look over your shoulders to check your blind spots.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check for vehicles only in the direction that you plan on going, then proceed.
Let all vehicles that arrive before or after you go first.
Check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, you must come to a full stop. Check for traffic in all directions before driving forward.

questions.question: Drivers turning left must yield to:

options.text: Overtaking cars.
Oncoming cars.
No one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming cars.
questions.explanation: If you are turning left, yield to oncoming vehicles driving straight. Only turn left when it is safe and you will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Drivers are required to obey instructions from:

options.text: Security guards patrolling parking lots.
Other drivers whose vehicles are broken down on the roadway.
Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.
questions.explanation: You must obey flaggers at construction sites. They control traffic to keep drivers and workers safe.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, it is safe to return to your lane if you:

options.text: Cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
Have passed the other vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to your lane after passing, make sure you are not too close to the vehicle you passed. When you see both headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough space to change lanes safely.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires float on water instead of gripping the road. How can you prevent hydroplaning in rain?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down in the rain to prevent hydroplaning. Driving fast can cause your tires to float on water and lose contact with the road, making your vehicle hard to control.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left at an intersection, always let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first. You can complete your turn once the intersection is clear and the signal allows it.

questions.question: The center line has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line. If the broken line is next to your lane, it means:

options.text: You cannot pass other vehicles in this area.
You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
You can only make right turns in this area.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
questions.explanation: When there is a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line, you can pass from the side with the broken line.

questions.question: What does this yellow sign mean?

options.text: One lane ahead.
Traffic will merge ahead.
Lane ends ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic will merge ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic may merge into your lane.

questions.question: What is the correct way to make a right turn?

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the center line before turning.
Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
Stay near the right curb as you approach, then move toward the middle of the street before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
questions.explanation: Before turning right, signal to warn other drivers. Slow down and stay as close as possible to the right curb or edge of the road.

questions.question: What does this white sign mean?

options.text: The railroad crossing is controlled. Keep your regular speed.
Look and listen, and be ready to stop if needed.
Stop at the tracks and wait for a signal before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look and listen, and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing, look and listen carefully. Slow down and be ready to stop. Wait for any trains to pass before you cross.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect your driving ability?

options.text: Three
Two
One

questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Do not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol. Even one drink will affect your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: At an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you must:

options.text: Wait for the green light before going.
Slow down and cross carefully.
Stop before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be more careful. Watch for other traffic and pedestrians as you cross.

questions.question: What is the speed limit near a school crossing?

options.text: 10 mph
15 mph
25 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 15 mph
questions.explanation: When no other speed limit is posted, you must drive 15 mph near a school crosswalk.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the car.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked vehicle, you must leave a note on it with your name, phone number, and address.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must drive through the intersection at this speed.
The top speed in good conditions is 55 mph.
You must not drive slower than 55 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: The top speed in good conditions is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the maximum speed limit for that road under good conditions. You can drive slower based on weather or traffic, but you cannot drive faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the right and slow down.
Move to the right and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: Let emergency vehicles pass by moving to the right edge of the road and stopping. If you are in an intersection, drive through first, then stop.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, what should you do?

options.text: Use low beam headlights.
Use high beam headlights until you are 10 feet away.
Use high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when following another car. Use high beams only in rural areas when other cars are far away.

questions.question: At sunrise, sunset, rain, or snow, it is hard to see and be seen. How can you let other drivers know you are there?

options.text: Turn up the dashboard lights.
Turn on your parking lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights when it is hard to see or be seen. Always use low beam headlights if you need to use your wipers.

questions.question: A blood alcohol level of 0.02 percent:

options.text: Has no effect on your driving.
Does not put other drivers at risk.
Doubles your chance of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doubles your chance of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Each 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol level nearly doubles the risk of a fatal accident.
